title: fNIRS temporal resolution limits
bottleneck: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy measures brain blood flow non-invasively, but hemodynamic responses lag neural activity by seconds, making fNIRS useless for real-time control. Spatial resolution is coarse, depth penetration limited to cortex surface, and hair blocks optical signals. It's a slow, shallow window into the brain.
why_it_blocks: fNIRS's safety and portability would make it ideal for everyday BCIs, but its seconds-long lag rules out interactive use. Speed of blood is the fundamental limit.
current_state: Wearable fNIRS headsets serve research on cognitive workload and are improving. Real-time BCI control via hemodynamics remains infeasible. Blood-flow responses peak seconds after neural activity, so any control loop built on fNIRS is inherently too slow for interaction. Hybrid EEG-fNIRS systems inherit the weaknesses of both, EEG noise and hemodynamic lag, with little synergy to show for it.
